name: templates-dir-validation
body: Templates dir validation: before any deck validation, render or serve (startup and every reload), kalide validates the project's `templates/` directory, fail-fast in a fixed order: (1) `library.yaml` present and valid; (2) layout (templates-dir-layout: only library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/, media/ at top level; template names unique across slides/ and sections/); (3) each template in kind-then-name order (slides/ then sections/): `template.yaml`, `layout.html.tmpl`, `example.md` present, `template.yaml` well-formed against the schema vocabulary with no `usage:` key, layout parses as standard html/template with the documented function set (template-language), parse errors file:line-qualified; (4) the template-build-checks across the set; (5) each theme in name order has `theme.css`; (6) references resolve: every relative url(…) in a theme's `theme.css` resolves to an existing file inside that theme's directory `templates/themes/<name>/`; every relative src/href in layouts resolves to an existing file inside `templates/`; and every `media "path"` argument in a layout is a relative path (not absolute, no `..` segments) naming an existing file under `templates/media/` — a violation is a templates error qualified with the layout's file:line; (7) each example.md validates against its template and its layout executes (execute errors file:line-qualified). The first failure is reported as a templates error: path-qualified (e.g. `templates/slides/content/template.yaml:12`), with a hint and closest-match suggestion where applicable, in the terminal at startup and in the full-page error on reload — the same error-reporting format as deck errors, labelled as a templates error. AC: one test per step shows the expected first error (step 6 includes a missing `media` file, a `..` argument and an absolute argument); a valid dir proceeds to deck validation.
